plates.quality_reason: Quality: readable faces (Kary Mullis driving along Highway 128 through the California redwoods in April 1983 conceiving exponential PCR primer doubling, dissolving to Randall Saiki, Henry Erlich, and Mullis at Cetus Corporation in 1985–1988 replacing boiled E. coli enzyme with Yellowstone Taq polymerase).

plates.side_label: 1985 MANUAL KLENOW PCR (OPEN TUBE EVERY 95 °C CYCLE) VS 1988 AUTOMATED CLOSED-TUBE YELLOWSTONE TAQ PCR (10^6–10^9×)
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked E. coli Klenow vs Taq PCR automation chart from Saiki et al. & Mullis (20 Dec 1985 Science 230: 1350–1354 & 29 Jan 1988 Science 239: 487–491) shows manual enzyme addition required at every 95 °C cycle with E. coli polymerase vs continuous closed-tube 30-cycle exponential amplification (10^6 to 10^9-fold specificity at 72 °C) with Yellowstone Taq polymerase.

teach_overlay.label: 1985 MANUAL E. COLI PCR (30 ENZYME ADDITIONS) VS 1988 CLOSED-TUBE TAQ PCR (2^30 = 1.07B COPIES)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked E. coli Klenow vs Taq PCR automation chart on period paper from Saiki et al. & Mullis (20 Dec 1985 Science 230: 1350–1354 & 29 Jan 1988 Science 239: 487–491) showing manual enzyme addition required at every 95 °C cycle with E. coli polymerase vs continuous closed-tube 30-cycle exponential amplification (10^6 to 10^9-fold specificity at 72 °C) with Yellowstone Taq polymerase
teach_overlay.scale: doubling one molecule thirty times in a row is like folding a sheet of paper thirty times — it grows from a single invisible strand into more than a billion copies inside a droplet smaller than a teardrop
